threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think waiting 15 minutes for a bus is a nightmare. Welcome to Hackney, where it’s just a warm-up.
Saw a bloke on the 196 last night, passionately arguing with a lamppost about the merits of pineapple on pizza. The lamppost stayed silent.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a full business suit selling homemade falafel outside the Rathaus Neukölln. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can find a street art installation that changes weekly, making every walk feel like a mini-gallery tour. Never seen that anywhere else!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know the best alley for taco trucks—while tourists are stuck at that one crowded spot on Mission.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy in a full tuxedo get on the 31 while juggling a bouquet. Just another Friday night in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar is a tapas bar; they miss out on the local vermouth spots where you get olives and a real vibe, not just the usual pinchos.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they insist on saying 'Hola' to every single doorman like it’s a personal greeting. Locals just nod and move on.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a ‘cold pint’ means anything other than warm lager that costs a fiver in a pub full of hipsters.
Last night on the 59 bus, a guy serenaded a couple with 'Wonderwall' while another was having a heated debate about whether pineapple belongs on pizza.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting at Hermannplatz, I saw a group of kids playing in the fountain, while a man smoked a cigarette, totally unfazed by the chaos. That’s when it hit me—this is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a massive outdoor flea market where you can buy vintage vinyl, freshly grilled sausages, and hand-carved wooden toys, all while listening to a live jazz band.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they casually mention how the BART's delays are just another Tuesday. Outsiders act surprised—it’s all part of the commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a bus driver calmly handle a fight between two riders while still keeping time on his route. That’s the real transit artistry of Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all bars are open late; meanwhile, many locals have their last caña by 11 PM, preferring the quiet of home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still take photos of their food at local tapas bars and ask if the sangria is made with red or white wine.
